evals.prompt:
Revise the plan below from the feedback below it. Two comments are unresolved, and I need a traceable result rather than an overwrite.

Plan: cap request rate on packages/api
  Objective: reject traffic over a per-route ceiling before it reaches handlers.
  Tasks: (1) add a token-bucket middleware, (2) make the ceiling configurable per
  route, (3) return 429 with a Retry-After header, (4) add load-shedding metrics.
  Success criteria: requests over the limit return 429; the limit is configurable
  per route; existing routes keep current behaviour; p99 latency unchanged.
  Validation: unit tests for the bucket, an integration test per route group.

Feedback:
  1. "Retry-After is not in the success criteria, either drop it from the tasks or add the criterion."
  2. "Unresolved: do we shed load per route or per client? The plan assumes per route without saying so."
  3. "Unresolved: no criterion covers what happens when the bucket store is unavailable."
Work only from the text above; do not read or edit any files.
assertions: Every feedback item receives an applied, deferred, rejected, unresolved, or scope-change disposition with rationale
The output preserves the source and returns a distinct revised plan without assigning approval semantics to status

evals.prompt: Plan: scope is reader backpressure; the criterion is no dropped rows; the estimate is 8 days. Feedback: 1. cover the replay producer too. 2. ship this week. Revise the plan.
assertions: Each feedback item gets a disposition (applied, deferred, rejected, unresolved question, or scope change) with a rationale
The accepted change is propagated through scope, risks, and criteria, and the source revision is preserved beside the new one

assertions: The materially conflicting instructions are enumerated and the revision stops on the conflict instead of averaging it away
